title: Truth and Divine Mercy
english: Truth is spoken of in the Savior and in the [psalm where] God sent His mercy and His truth and rescued my soul from the midst of troubles (Ps 117:1). Thus truth and the hope of the nations are one; therefore, having shone upon the human race, it calls all the nations and all the peoples, teaching [them] to give thanks to the Father who strengthens His mercy and makes His truth remain unto the age.

Since God is good and wills the repentance of the sinner rather than his death, you who are responsible for sin, by performing confession through repentance upon him, you will have him forgiving those for whom you confess. For His mercy is found inseparable from Him unto the age, since it is always [so]; in His mercy, not only now but also formerly from the beginning, all those having experience of His goodness confess to Him.

A righteous man having become in affliction does not so much entreat to be outside of it, but how to bravely and cheerfully bear it (Ps 117:5-9). For indeed the one being distressed in the stadium against opponents does not wish the contest to pass by him, lest he become exhausted, but entreats the trainer to cooperate with him, so that, enduring the things brought by the adversary with hope of victory and crown, the things through which the crown is awarded may seem gentle to him.

And it is possible to say different things concerning mortals, 'I shall not fear what man shall do to me' (Ps 117:6), but concerning invisible enemies, 'I also shall see my enemies' (Ps 117:7); for some enemies are even the men who rise up against us, waging war against us and setting themselves against us lethally. And if 'I shall not fear what man shall do to me' is also referred to the devil, on account of 'An enemy, a man, did this' (Matt 13:28)—for it is clear that [he did] the sowing of the tares—and 'But you are man and not God: visit' (Ezek 28:2).

'It is good to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man' (Ps 117:8), and the following: it is not that trusting and hoping in the Lord is good only when compared with trusting in man and hoping in rulers. For this is simply and properly good.

But to trust and hope in man and ruler is not good; rather, such instruction is brought to those who are eager to trust in man and hope in a ruler, that they may learn to trust in the ever-abiding and strong and almighty God, and not in mortal man, easily corrupted.

And sometimes he is also double-minded in intention; for instead of helping, sometimes he will also greatly harm the one who trusts in him; therefore blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord, remaining unashamed, according to 'In you, Lord, I hoped; let me not be ashamed unto the age' (Ps 30:2).

Ps 117:10-13: If it is not said hyperbolically, what is promised is impossible; for how did all the nations surround one man dwelling in Judea, warring as they surrounded him, and he defended himself against them in the name of the Lord?
For it becomes weapon and shield and fortress to the one who wears it.

But consider whether it is not possible to understand the things set before us similarly to the 'In the mornings I slew all the sinners of the earth' (Ps 100:8), by the serious man being surrounded by evil spirits suggesting the titillations of the flesh and the other passions with all the works of the flesh, and moreover godless words refuting with sophistic cleverness the doctrines of the truth.
But the well-strung and strong one, armed with the appellation of God, shall overthrow all the nations, turning them to flight, and sometimes even destroying them.
For the one who instead of weapon and sword used the name of God shall cut off the passionate impulses along with the troubled reasonings, but also loosing and overthrowing the [...].
